overview: Porthcothan is a sandy, sheltered beach at the head of a narrow inlet between Newquay and Padstow, with a small village behind. It’s popular with families and surfers, with lifeguards on duty during summer days, and surf schools run lessons here from time to time.
Like many Cornish coves it has its smuggling stories, and the coast path north and south passes a string of quieter coves and headlands.

expect.title: Family beach
expect.text: A sandy beach patrolled by lifeguards in the summer daytime.

expect.title: Surf lessons
expect.text: Surf schools sometimes teach here, so it’s a handy place for a first lesson.

expect.title: Coast path
expect.text: Walk north to Fox Cove and Treyarnon or south towards Bedruthan.

goodToKnow.label: Facilities
goodToKnow.text: There’s a paid car park by the beach and a little shop for supplies.

week.text: An easy, sheltered family beach on the north coast, handy for Padstow. It faces north-west, so evenings are lovely, and Macdonald’s Farm nearby is a good add-on with young children.

pairWith.why: a sandy surf beach a short way north

tips: Walk the coast path north to Fox Cove for a quieter spot.
